Both pages read September 8, 2026. 2026-08-01 (v2.1.0): all prices removed - see price_removal. The 97 expansion rows lost their fields at v2.0.0; the 29 pre-expansion rows followed the same day after review of their mixed retailer provenance. The removed figures were live Amazon.com street prices observed 2026-07-29; the rows' specifications and their 'source' specification-page URLs are unchanged and remain individually verifiable. Original expansion record: 97 parts added and one retired on 2026-07-29 (30 -> 126 parts); every added row carries a 'source' field naming the manufacturer, Newegg or B&H specification page its specs were read from; any candidate whose specs could not be confirmed against a page that was actually retrieved was dropped rather than estimated (41 candidates dropped); several vendor sites (TechPowerUp, Kingston, Crucial, MSI, Gigabyte, Zotac, PNY, AMD product pages) refused automated retrieval, so those brands are under-represented and NVIDIA add-in-board rows skew toward ASUS; PCIe lane counts are recorded only where a retrieved page stated them explicitly. Original pre-expansion sourcing: manufacturer pages, TechPowerUp, Tom's Hardware, and verified retailer listings. Performance tier estimates are TechFuelHQ editorial assessments based on aggregate review consensus, not first-party benchmarks (except where the part appears in a TechFuelHQ Open Bench Dataset, in which case the tier is anchored to first-party data). 2026-08-30: Intel K-SKU tdp_w changed from Processor Base Power to Maximum Turbo Power. The PC Builder sums tdp_w as the power the chip actually draws, and every K-SKU held the 125 W base figure, so PSU sizing ran a retail size light. Values are Intel's published MTP. Non-K Intel rows (Core Ultra 5 225/225F, 65 W base) were NOT changed - their MTP was not verified in this pass and is recorded as open rather than guessed. 2026-09-29 correction (v2.1.1): every AM5 CPU's supported_chipsets now lists all AM5 chipsets AMD names (X870E, X870, B850, B840, X670E, X670, A620, A620A, plus B650). AMD's AM5 chipset page says all Socket AM5 motherboards are compatible with all Socket AM5 processors, with a BIOS update possibly required for Ryzen 8000 and 9000 on 600-series boards (https://www.amd.com/en/products/processors/chipsets/am5.html, read 2026-09-29). The old four-chipset list made the PC Builder flag every AM5 CPU on the A620A board as incompatible. 2026-11-18 (v2.1.2): added power_draw_w, power_draw_basis and power_draw_note to every component model. Power values are stock/peak DC planning values, not average wall-socket measurements. CPU values use Intel MTP where available and estimated AMD PPT; GPU values use the model TGP/TBP; motherboard, RAM, storage and included case-fan values are explicitly marked estimates. PSU power_draw_w is null because PSU input draw is load- and efficiency-dependent.
compatibility_rules: CPU and motherboard must share socket (AM5, LGA1851, LGA1700)
Motherboard chipset must be in cpu.supported_chipsets (e.g. AM5 X870E supports Ryzen 7000+9000; B650 supports Ryzen 7000+9000 with BIOS update)
Motherboard ram_type must match RAM ram_type (DDR5 only at this generation)

PSU wattage must exceed the sum of power_draw_w for the selected CPU, GPU, motherboard, RAM, storage and case, plus 30W reserve for an unlisted CPU cooler/pump, extra fans and peripherals; then keep a 20% sizing margin. PSU power_draw_w is null and is not added to the load.
Case form_factor must accept motherboard form_factor (ATX > mATX > ITX)
Case max_gpu_length_mm must exceed GPU length_mm
Storage interface (NVMe Gen5 / Gen4 / SATA) must match a free motherboard slot

power_draw_model.meaning: Estimated maximum DC-side power contribution at stock settings for PSU sizing; not average gaming draw and not AC wall-socket draw.
power_draw_model.cpu: Intel uses published Maximum Turbo Power where available. AMD uses an estimated stock PPT of approximately 1.35 × rated TDP. CPU values are package power, not TDP labels.
power_draw_model.gpu: Uses the TGP/TBP value recorded for that exact model. Partner-card limits and manual overclocking may differ.
power_draw_model.motherboard: Model-specific planning estimate for board electronics and VRM losses; excludes CPU, GPU, memory and storage.
power_draw_model.ram: Planning estimate for the complete memory kit, including RGB where fitted.
power_draw_model.storage: Peak-active planning estimate for the particular SSD model/capacity.
power_draw_model.case: Includes estimated power for factory-installed case fans only. Chassis itself draws no power; separately added fans are not included.
power_draw_model.psu: null because the PSU is not a fixed load. AC wall input can be estimated as total DC load divided by PSU efficiency at that load.
power_draw_model.important: Estimated values are suitable for initial compatibility and PSU sizing, not for precise electrical measurement. Cooler/pump, extra fans, USB-powered devices and other unlisted parts need to be accounted for separately.
